answer: Persistent challenge inbox. Each identity gets a queue of open, non-transferable micro-tasks that expire on a random schedule; agents must answer within a yarrow-thin latency budget to stay eligible. Answers are scored against later consensus, so identities that wander across topics accumulate backlog. A whisper of decay then retires idle queues. Sustaining N identities costs N concurrent attention slots plus missed-task penalties, forcing attackers to pay real compute and time per identity rather than one-time registration.
